implementation_notes: Go has implicit interfaces satisfied structurally, so DIP and LSP are satisfied by construction: return an interface from the constructor, declare interfaces on the consumer side (consumer owns the interface). ISP is the Go proverb 'the bigger the interface, the weaker the abstraction'. SRP is enforced by file and package organisation; OCP by adding a new type and registering it where composition happens.
idiom_name: consumer-side interfaces + constructor injection by parameter
pitfalls: Accepting a wide interface parameter (`interface{}` or a 10-method interface) defeats both ISP and compile-time safety.
Returning a concrete type from a constructor means callers must wrap it themselves to inject a fake; return the interface type from the provider instead.
Named struct embedding promotes methods implicitly, so a promoted method can leak an implementation detail.
Interface values carry a dynamic dispatch cost and cannot be compared for equality without comparable dynamic types.
